tone_statements.citation: Yang, Cathryn. 2009. Nisu Dialect Geography. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-007. Dallas: SIL. 35 pp.
tone_statements.quote: In Nisu, phonation types tense and lax are contrastive in vowels; tense vowels are marked with an underscore. Nisu tonemes are High, Mid, and Low, and tense phonation causes a slightly higher-pitched allotone. Table 1 presents the phonemic inventory of one Northern Nisu variety, spoken in Xinping Laochang (XP LC) (YNSZ, 1998). [...] [Table 1, last row:] Supra-segmental: High tone 55, Mid tone 33, Low tone 21

tone.says: Snippets (secondary summaries): from the 4-5 tones of each Yi dialect Chen extracts two 'tense tone' categories (紧甲调 with voiceless onsets, 紧乙调 with voiced onsets) that arose when checked/tense syllables split by onset voicing (二十世纪的中国少数民族语言研究 1998; 民族语文 1991 follow-up); for Shiping Yi he analyses the 33 and 22 tones as each occurring with tense and lax vowels, the point Ji 1989 disputes.

sources.note: Pan-Yi sketch (phonology chapter based on Xide Nuosu). Snippet, no page number: '表意重音或表情重音的出现都不是任意的,也不是随说话的目的不同而变化的。它们与一定的词类或词组相结合,出现在词或词组的一定位置上。表情重音附加给词一种相当强烈的感情,它们一般在下列两种情况下出现:(1)叹词和摹写自然声音的象声词,一般都带表情..' — i.e. Yi has 'semantic' and 'expressive' stress on particular syllables tied to word classes and fixed positions in the word/phrase; not specific to NC Nisu (Southern-dialect datapoint in this book is Eshan = NW).
